topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic contains the introductory framing, course overview, and learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Biological foundations, tissue architecture, and cell culture models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as an accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes causing a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms, routes, and histological manifestations of tumor invasion and metastasis, focusing on distinguishing benign from malignant lesions.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature, clinical dangers, and mechanisms of mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the standard naming systems for tumors and the physical and physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant growths cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence in humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence across human populations and diverse animal species as a feature of multicellularity.

topics.label: Clinical cancer screening modalities and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, clinical successes, and practical limitations of population screening methods across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the concluding summary and administrative framing for upcoming practical sessions.
